newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Nicolaas Wegter announced a conference on the role of the media in the peace process in Ex-Yougoslavia on November 29. He asked EU journalists to book beforehand as there was a limited number of seats.
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said there would be a briefing on the fourth meeting of the EU/Andes joint commission with the two heads of delegation at 1800/1700 at the Borschette Centre.
He said there would be a briefing on Commissioner Padraig Flynn's visit in Spain at 1300/1200 GMT on Thursday.
He added that South African Vice-President Thabo Mbeki would meet Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro on Thursday and would meet journalists at 1545/1445 GMT for pictures and questions.
Vale de Almeida announced a draft Commmission directive to continue to limit the import of some alcohols and tobacco for personal use into Denmark, Finland and Sweden.

Spokesman Willy Helin briefed on Thursday's Industry Council. He said the main points on the agenda concerning competition were the new code on metallurgy aids, state aids, steel monitoring and mergers and acquisition regulations.

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas briefed on the Commission's weekly meeting in retransmission from Strasbourg. He said the Commission had decided not to admit genetically modified maize without the awaited scientific advice and had urged the concerned scientific committees to work as quickly as possible.
Van der Pas added that Commission President Jacques Santer had said that the Commission should need an orientation debate on genetically modified products in general in the near future.

Van der Pas said the Commission had had an orientation debate on tobacco. He said Santer had asked Commissionners Hanz Fischler and Padraig Flynn to make concrete proposals in the light of health and social issues related to the fight against tobacco. No date has been fixed yet, he said.
Van der Pas also said that President Santer had answered U.K. Prime Minister John Major's letter on the working time directive.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/1014: Conference on the role of the media in the peace process in Ex-Yougoslavia.
- IP/96/1015: Commission proposes strategy to remove technical barriers to trade for European exporters.
- IP/96/1016: Phare and Tacis democracy programme 1996.
- IP/96/1017: The Commission launches a 50 million ecu action plan on research into BSE.
- IP/96/1018: Commission proposes renewed ceilings for EIB lending to third countries.
- IP/96/1019: European Commission approves draft negotating mandate for accession to a new-look Eurocontrol.
- IP/96/1020: The European Commission will not admit genetically modified maize without scientific advice.
- IP/96/1021: Travellers customs exceptions - Commission suggests derogations for Denmark, Finland and Sweden.
- Oil Bulletin No844.
- Selling prices of petroleum products in US dollars and in ECUs.
- Eurostat, Statistics in focus, agriculture, forestry and fisheries No12-1196: Trends in the EU agricultural price indices in the second quarter of 1996.
- ME96/13.11: Midday express.
